claim: Using a headline database to classify large individual-stock price moves as accompanied by identifiable public news or not: stocks with bad public news show significant negative drift for up to 12 months (slow reaction/underreaction); stocks with a large move and NO identifiable news tend to reverse the following month (overreaction to a non-fundamental move); both hold controlling for size/book-to-market; the no-news reversal is concentrated in smaller, more illiquid stocks and weakens (does not vanish) once low-priced stocks are excluded.
quote: Original sample predates 2000; no post-2015 magnitude figure in the abstract.
limitations: Abstract-level only, ScienceDirect full text paywalled; sample predates 2000, no post-2015 magnitude figure in the abstract; 'no news' means 'no headline in Chan's database', approximated here by news_packets + 8-K item-2.02 coverage, not reproduced exactly.
independent_replication: Corroborated qualitatively by Savor (2012, different information proxy) and Dyl/Yuksel/Zaynutdinova (2019, same headline/announcement framing, sample extended to 2015); no post-2020 independent replication found this pass.
impact_on_spec: Grounds this iteration's event definition (large market-adjusted drop, PIT news-vs-no-news classification) and the expectation that any local effect is likely concentrated in smaller/less liquid names within the top-1500 ADV universe.

claim: Using analyst-report activity as an information proxy around major one-day price shocks: shocks accompanied by information are followed by drift (continuation); shocks without information are followed by reversal; investors underreact to fundamental news and overreact to non-fundamental shocks; information-based changes correlate more with future earnings surprises; drift requires the price move and analyst-recommendation change to share sign.
quote: Drift is present only when the direction of the price move and the change in analyst recommendations have the same sign.
limitations: Abstract/summary-level only; SSRN and ScienceDirect both returned HTTP 403 on WebFetch this pass; uses analyst reports as the information proxy, not raw headlines/8-K filings, so it is a methodologically distinct but conceptually parallel test to Chan (2003).
independent_replication: Same qualitative conclusion as Chan (2003) via a different identification method; treated as corroborating, not independent proof for our specific PIT news classification.
impact_on_spec: Second, methodologically distinct source behind the same brief mechanism; supports testing both the no-news-reversal leg and the bad-news-drift (short) leg as economically motivated, not ad hoc.

claim: Independent replication of the Chan/Savor mechanism on extreme one-day price changes, sample 1986-2015: investors overreact to non-information-based price movements (reversal) and underreact to firm-specific public announcements (continuation/drift); effects concentrated in smaller firms and firms with lower institutional ownership, where the magnitude is also larger; liquidity improvement following the post-decimalization period reduced the magnitude of BOTH reversals and continuations -- a documented decay in effect size as market microstructure improved, over a sample ending a decade before this iteration's TEST window.
quote: No claim in this source about the 2020s.
limitations: Abstract-level synthesis only via WebSearch; ScienceDirect and SSRN both returned HTTP 403 on WebFetch; exact quantitative magnitudes (percent, t-stats) not independently read from primary text. This is the newest (2015-sample) replication found in 3 targeted WebSearch queries this pass; no post-2020 independent replication exists in the located evidence.
independent_replication: This IS the independent replication (of Chan 2003 / Savor 2012), located via WebSearch this pass; not itself yet independently re-replicated post-2020.
impact_on_spec: Sets honest priors: the decay finding (magnitude shrinks with liquidity improvement, decimalization) argues AGAINST assuming Chan (2003)-era magnitudes still hold in the far-more-liquid, more-algorithmic 2024-2026 TEST window; this iteration measures the current-window magnitude directly rather than assuming persistence, consistent with the mission's ban on assuming durability without evidence.
